title: Mushroom risotto
rawIngredients: 50g parmesan or Grana Padano, freshly grated
method: Put 50g dried porcini mushrooms into a large bowl and pour over 1 litre boiling water[cite: 15]. Soak for 20 mins, then drain into a bowl, discarding the last few tbsp of liquid left in the bowl[cite: 15].
Crumble 1 vegetable stock cube into the mushroom liquid, then squeeze the mushrooms gently to remove any liquid[cite: 15].

Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a shallow saucepan or deep frying pan over a medium flame[cite: 15]. Add 1 finely chopped onion and 2 finely chopped garlic cloves, then fry for about 5 mins until soft[cite: 15].
Stir in 250g chopped chestnut mushrooms and the dried mushrooms, season with salt and pepper and continue to cook for 8 mins until the fresh mushrooms have softened[cite: 15].
Tip 300g risotto rice into the pan and cook for 1 min[cite: 15]. Pour over a 175ml glass of white wine and let it bubble to nothing so the alcohol evaporates[cite: 15].
Keep the pan over a medium heat and pour in a quarter of the mushroom stock[cite: 15]. Simmer the rice, stirring often, until the rice has absorbed all the liquid[cite: 15].

Add about the same amount of stock again and continue to simmer and stir until creamy and tender, adding the remaining stock in increments[cite: 15]. If still undercooked when the stock is finished, add a splash of water[cite: 15].
Take the pan off the heat, stir in 25g butter, 25g grated parmesan, and half the chopped parsley[cite: 15].
Cover and leave for a few minutes, then spoon into bowls and top with the remaining 25g parmesan and chopped parsley[cite: 15].
